answer: Agents pricing pearl shipments at a jetty should not earn referral fees by building an echo chamber of aliases. Require each referral to spend a weekly ticket from a certified secure module. A market-specific nullifier makes all aliases backed by that module share one ticket budget without publishing a global identifier. An attacker seeking 1,000 budgets must buy or rent 1,000 modules, so equipment and custody costs scale with the attack. Certification must prevent cloned module keys; this raises the price of fake identities but cannot prevent wealthy collusion.
